summary: All 36 repeated-value rating clusters (417 records) are formula/template-generated, proven by identical per-key offset profiles shared across clusters of the same category (10 nature clusters share offsets [-0.2,+0.1,-0.6,-0.9,-1.1,+0.3,+0.1,-0.1,+0.2]; 8 castle clusters share [-0.2,-0.3,-0.7,-1.0,-0.9,+0.3,-0.5,-0.1,+0.2]; 5 POI clusters are arithmetic staircases; 3 are near-flat). 62 records inside clusters carry laundered {manual, high} metadata from a bulk 'Coordinate Calibration' pass (Stage 3 PR 12A Kanto editorial) applied to identical template vectors; by contrast all 77 high/manual records OUTSIDE clusters have distinct vectors (genuine per-record review). Hubs (role=hub, kind=city/ward/town/village) are scored like individual attractions: 114 cities share a 'perfect' 9.5 vector, 44 stamped high-confidence, displayed raw everywhere and driving 'Highly recommended by other travelers' claims. 336 records lack ratingMetadata entirely; the confidence gate (0.5) protects SCORING but not DISPLAY, which renders ratings.overall raw at 7+ sites. Root cause code-proven: scripts/expand-major-city-catalog.ts:375-379,478-491 generates ratings from a deterministic hash (6.2+(hash%34)/10) - same hash feeds season scores (AgentD corroboration). At least three mechanisms: (1) hash generator (v1.9.2 expansion, mostly distinct vectors), (2) older template-profile generators (the 36 clusters), (3) Kanto bulk 'Coordinate Calibration' stamping 139 records manual/high - 62 on identical template vectors (laundered), 77 outside clusters (70 consistent with real review; 7 suspect: hash-generated seasons).

hubScoringFinding.finding: Hubs are scored like individual attractions. 114 city/ward/town records share the identical vector {overall 9.5, couple 9.3, summer 9, winter 9.1, rain 9.2, food 9.6, photography 9.5, relaxation 9.2, value 9.4, uniqueness 9.4} asserting a city-wide overall of 9.5 with food 9.6. 44 of them carry {rubricVersion:2, method:manual, confidence:high} stamped by a bulk pass whose only source is the generic gotokyo.org Tokyo/Saitama/Kanagawa index page (same URL for all 22 Tokyo wards) and whose changeSummary literally reads 'Coordinate Calibration'. 18 of the 114 additionally have status=verified yet no ratingMetadata. A city rating cannot be a single per-attraction score; the rubric (REQUIRED_RATING_KEYS, per-attraction dimensions like food/photography) does not fit whole-city granularity.
hubScoringFinding.evidence: identical vector across 114 distinct cities; identical generic tourism_board source for all stamped records; changeSummary 'Stage 3 PR 12A Kanto Editorial Review & Coordinate Calibration'; control group: 77 outside-cluster manual/high records all have distinct vectors, proving real review produces distinct vectors.
hubScoringFinding.recommendation: Do not display a raw overall score for role=hub records until per-city rating evidence exists; treat hub scores as editorial-review-pending in Phase 2 (remove ratings or gate display).

displayChangeSpec.productQuestion: Should a raw Overall Score be displayed as authoritative for unverified/template ratings?
displayChangeSpec.answer: No. Every score-render site displays ratings.overall raw with no confidence gating: a template 9.5 hub renders as a perfect score and RecommendationExplainability emits 'Highly recommended by other travelers' (overall>=8.5) with zero evidence. The scoring layer already gates by confidence (ratingReliability: high 1.0 / medium 0.8 / low 0.5 / missing 0.5, REC-001); the display layer does not. Smallest safe change: gate score presentation and the traveler claim on ratingMetadata confidence (high/medium = show; low or missing = 'Under editorial review' placeholder), and extend the existing editorialReviewPending disclosure to missing metadata.

'under-review' : 'verified'; }

rootCause.mechanism1_hashGenerator: scripts/expand-major-city-catalog.ts (npm run expand:major-city-catalog) rating() at lines 375-379: hash = dimension*97 then (hash*31+charCode)>>>0 per char of seed; returns 6.2+(hash%34)/10. Ratings at lines 478-491: overall=rating('parent.id:name',0), couple..uniqueness=rating(id,1..9), plus family/accessibility (id,10..11). Same hash feeds season/crowd/comfort (AgentD: 291 fractional-season records). Corroborates AgentD_SeasonCrowdDuration finding.
rootCause.mechanism2_templateProfiles: Earlier template generator(s) produced the 36 repeated-value clusters: per-category fixed offset profiles (nature, castle, staircase, flat, extreme-divergence) with category base values 7.2-9.5. Cluster members share EXACT identical 10-key vectors across distinct ids - impossible from the per-id hash (mechanism 1) and impossible from real review.
rootCause.mechanism3_coordinateCalibration: 'Stage 3 PR 12A Kanto Editorial Review & Coordinate Calibration' bulk pass stamped 139 records {rubricVersion:2, method:manual, confidence:high}. 62 of them sit inside clusters on identical template vectors (laundered). 77 outside clusters have distinct vectors: 70 are consistent with genuine per-record review (distinct vectors + non-fractional seasons + specific official sources); 7 are suspect because their season data is hash-generated: boso-no-mura, hachioji-castle-tokyo, katori-jingu, nikko-toshogu-shrine-tochigi, tama-zoological-park, ueno-zoo, yokohama-zoorasia (fractional season scores from the hash script - stamps unsupported).
rootCause.note: The staircase/extreme-divergence clusters (23,25,28,29,30,31,33,35) show values below the hash floor 6.2 (e.g. rain 6.0, food 6.1) so they come from a variant/older generator, not the exact v1.9.2 function; the 29 fractional-season in-cluster ids above corroborate hash-script provenance for those clusters. AgentD alignment: nikko-toshogu-shrine-tochigi (overall 9.9) and hachioji-castle-tokyo (9.8) exceed the v1.9.2 hash max 6.2+33/10=9.5, so a variant/extension of the hash generator exists (higher floor or different modulus) - the hash-script family, not the exact v1.9.2 function, is the provenance for those records. All 7 suspect manual/high stamps confirmed by AgentD (fractional seasons + pipeline 60/40 walking split).
